name: Document Upload and Processing
description: A pattern for services that accept document uploads from users, process them (scanning, validation, extraction, classification), and store them securely. Common in government for evidence submission, form uploads, identity verification, and bulk document ingestion workflows.
whenToUse: Services requiring citizens or staff to upload documents as part of a transaction
Evidence submission workflows where documents must be validated and classified
Identity verification processes requiring document scanning and data extraction
Bulk document ingestion from partner organisations or scanning operations
Services requiring OCR, text extraction, or automated document classification
whenNotToUse: Simple file sharing between known internal users (use SharePoint or equivalent)
Real-time video or audio streaming that is not document-based
Scenarios where documents are only stored and retrieved without processing
Small-scale file uploads where a simple form attachment would suffice
Document collaboration and co-editing scenarios (use productivity suites)

typicalComponents.name: Upload Service
typicalComponents.purpose: Accept file uploads with size limits, type validation, and progress tracking
typicalComponents.technology: Pre-signed URLs to S3/Blob Storage with API validation

typicalComponents.name: Malware Scanner
typicalComponents.purpose: Scan all uploaded files for viruses and malicious content before processing
typicalComponents.technology: ClamAV, Windows Defender, or cloud-native scanning

typicalComponents.name: Document Processor
typicalComponents.purpose: Extract text, metadata, and structured data from uploaded documents
typicalComponents.technology: Amazon Textract, Azure Form Recognizer, or Document AI

typicalComponents.name: Quarantine Storage
typicalComponents.purpose: Isolate uploaded files until scanning and validation is complete
typicalComponents.technology: Separate S3 bucket or Blob container with restricted access

typicalComponents.name: Clean Storage
typicalComponents.purpose: Store validated and processed documents with appropriate retention
typicalComponents.technology: S3, Azure Blob Storage, or Cloud Storage with lifecycle policies

typicalComponents.name: Processing Queue
typicalComponents.purpose: Decouple upload acceptance from async processing pipeline
typicalComponents.technology: SQS, Azure Queue Storage, or Pub/Sub

securityControls: Scan ALL uploaded files for malware before any processing or storage in clean buckets
Validate file types using magic bytes, not just file extensions
Implement file size limits appropriate to the use case
Store uploads in quarantine storage until scanning is complete
Encrypt all stored documents at rest with appropriate key management
Implement access controls ensuring only authorised services can read uploaded documents
Strip metadata from documents before serving to prevent information leakage
Implement content type validation to prevent polyglot file attacks
resilienceConsiderations: Use pre-signed URLs for direct-to-storage uploads to avoid application bottlenecks
Queue-based processing ensures uploads are not lost if processing services fail
Implement retry logic for document processing with dead letter queue for failures
Design for idempotent processing to handle duplicate uploads safely
Implement upload resumption for large files over unreliable connections
costConsiderations: Storage costs scale with document volume and retention period
AI/ML document processing services charge per page or per API call
Malware scanning costs per file scanned
Consider tiered storage for archived documents (infrequent access)
Processing compute costs only incurred during active document processing
Factor in the cost of manual review for documents that fail automated processing
operationalConsiderations: Monitoring for processing queue depth and failed document processing
Alerting for malware detections requiring investigation
Retention policy enforcement for document lifecycle management
Capacity planning for peak upload periods (e.g., deadline-driven submissions)
Manual review workflow for documents that fail automated validation
Regular updates to malware scanning signatures and processing models

services.name: Amazon S3
services.purpose: Document storage with pre-signed upload URLs

services.name: Amazon Textract
services.purpose: OCR and structured data extraction from documents

services.name: Amazon SQS
services.purpose: Processing queue for async document handling

services.name: Azure Blob Storage
services.purpose: Document storage with SAS token uploads

services.name: Cloud Storage
services.purpose: Document storage with signed URL uploads

services.name: Cloud DLP
services.purpose: Sensitive data detection in uploaded documents

questionsToAsk: What file types and maximum sizes need to be supported?
Is automated data extraction (OCR) required or just storage and retrieval?
What is the expected upload volume and are there peak periods?
What happens when a document fails validation — manual review or rejection?
What are the data retention requirements for uploaded documents?
Are there accessibility requirements for the upload interface (e.g., assistive technology support)?
commonMistakes: Not scanning uploads for malware, creating a vector for distributing malicious files
Validating file type by extension only, allowing disguised malicious files through
Processing uploads synchronously, causing timeouts for large files
Not implementing quarantine storage, allowing unscanned files to be accessed
Storing documents indefinitely without lifecycle policies, accumulating unnecessary costs
